notes: The second of the three Russian Hill district nominations of May 1987: eleven houses in eleven styles on one flat block of Green Street. The densest document of the three for named architects.

coverage.remaining: Nothing of 87002288. Still unread in this source: 89000319, the 68 listings certified 1990 or later, and 77000334, 01000281 and 100008228.
coverage.note: Russian Hill/Paris Block Architectural District (87002288, Anne Bloomfield, May 1987) read whole: 11 contributing houses and 1 non-contributing garage on the 1000 block of Green Street. 18 findings, every building represented: 9 architect credits (Hildebrand, Harris, Haupt, the Newsoms, Dutton, Hobart, Morgan, Foulkes, Wells & Livermore) plus dated moves, additions and remodels, and 1 notable past resident (Louis Feusier). Two credited names are printed wrong and published right — 'Oscar Kaupt' (spelled Haupt in the same entry) and 'L.B. Button' (Llewellyn B. Dutton, identified by the biography the entry gives). Owners not taken: the clients named for each house (a liquor dealer, a merchant tailor, a lumber clerk, a postman, a civil engineer, an importer), and the 1987 owners table; Charles M. Fickert is taken, as a public figure the nomination treats as the house's notable association.
